standard.title: Create and present informative and imaginative texts
standard.description: create and present spoken, written and multimodal informative and imaginative texts, manipulating language to suit context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create and present texts adapted for purpose and audience using cohesive devices and a range of sentence structures (AC9LCH6C05). They have created community-facing texts and performed imaginative work. They have not yet manipulated language for deliberate effect — through humour, persuasion, irony, stylistic experimentation — or produced extended multimodal texts with developed drafting and editing processes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and present spoken, written and multimodal informative and imaginative texts, manipulating language to suit context, purpose and audience — including persuasive, humorous and stylistically distinctive texts developed through drafting and editing.

nodes.label: Language manipulation for effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliberately manipulate language — through word choice, register variation, humour, persuasion, or stylistic devices — to create intended effects in a text.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a text demonstrating at least two deliberate language manipulation choices — for example, a persuasive structure, a humorous element, a register shift, or a descriptive device — and explain the intended effect of each.
nodes.typical_width: Manipulate language for deliberate effect — persuasive structures, humour, irony, descriptive and emotive language, jingles, wordplay; adapt characters and scenarios to new contexts; experiment with stylistic choices; discuss how language manipulation serves different purposes.
wider: Create two versions of the same content — one neutral, one manipulated for effect — and compare the impact of each on a reader or audience
Analyse how a published target language text manipulates language for effect, then apply the same technique in an original piece
nodes.hinge_reason: Language manipulation is the defining capability of this descriptor. Students who can only produce functional, neutral text cannot meet the 'manipulating language to suit context, purpose and audience' demand — which is the core distinction from Y5-6 text creation.

response_modes.reason: Language manipulation techniques — persuasion, humour, irony, stylistic variation — are built through encounter with varied models and repeated experimental production. Students need exposure to how published writers use these techniques before they can deploy them deliberately.

success_criteria: Produces a text with at least two deliberate language manipulation choices
Can explain the intended effect of each choice

nodes.label: Drafting, editing and stylistic development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop informative and imaginative texts through a drafting and editing process, making deliberate revisions to improve stylistic and creative features.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one text through a documented drafting process — showing at least two deliberate revisions that improve a stylistic or creative feature.
nodes.typical_width: Develop drafting and editing skills in own writing; revise texts for stylistic and creative improvement; seek and apply peer feedback; compare draft and final versions and explain revision choices; produce multimodal texts with developed visual and textual elements.
wider: Conduct a structured peer editing session — providing metalanguage-supported feedback on a peer's text and applying equivalent feedback to own work
Produce a portfolio of drafts showing the development of a single text from first draft to final version, with annotations explaining each revision decision

response_modes.reason: Effective drafting and editing requires students to evaluate their own texts analytically — identifying what is working and what needs revision — and to make deliberate improvements rather than surface corrections. Explicit revision frameworks and peer feedback structures build this self-evaluative capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Drafting and editing process is where the quality difference between adequate and excellent texts is made. Width investment here — structured revision cycles, peer editing, portfolio development — builds the reflective writing practice that produces genuinely polished work.
success_criteria: Produces a text through a documented drafting process with at least two deliberate revisions
Can explain the reason for each revision in terms of intended effect or audience impact

nodes.label: Extended multimodal presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create and present extended multimodal texts — combining spoken, written and visual elements — for informative or imaginative purposes, with appropriate production choices for context and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Create and present a multimodal text that combines at least two modes (spoken, written, visual) with deliberate production choices appropriate to purpose and audience.
nodes.typical_width: Produce multimodal presentations using tables, maps, charts, data visualisations; create promotional materials, travel texts, cultural commentaries; produce dramatic or humorous performances; write creative accounts of historical figures or characters; create captions, subtitles or commentary for video.
wider: Create a multimodal text for a real external audience — for example, a community publication, a school broadcast, or a digital production — and seek and incorporate feedback from that audience
Reflect on the production choices made in a multimodal text — explain how each mode contributes to meaning and why the combination is more effective than a single mode alone

response_modes.reason: Extended multimodal presentation integrates language manipulation (node 1) and drafting/editing skills (node 2) into a full production task. The teaching investment is in creating real presentation conditions — genuine audiences, real purposes — where production choices matter.

success_criteria: Creates a multimodal text combining at least two modes with deliberate production choices
Presents the text demonstrating awareness of audience through delivery or design choices
